summary: Burke County tower on a Georgia lookout list (older GFC list no. 101). A 1940 column on CCC tower land does not name this site. No later history found.

evidence.supports: Burke County location and older GFC list number 101
the older GFC list described 203 towers
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn).

evidence.supports: names for towers from number 73 on are the author's own creation
evidence.quote: For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.

evidence.supports: April 1940 donation of ten acres for the first CCC fire lookout tower in the county
evidence.quote: T.W. Mobley donated ten acres for the construction of the first fire lookout tower to be built in the county by the CCC.

evidence.supports: the column calls it the easternmost of five towers
evidence.quote: It would be the easternmost tower of the five to be constructed here.

evidence.supports: the column recalls news from April 11, 1940

corrections.proposed: gfc-101 (older Georgia Forestry Commission list number)
corrections.why: The source gives this number as gfc-101 from an older GFC list. No source gives the form 'US 101'.

notes_for_editor: Thin record, low confidence. Two sources only: the tnlandforms list (county, older GFC list number) and a 1940 'Looking Back' column that does not name the site. The column may describe a different tower. Girard (Burke County, NHLR gives 1940 as the build year) lies east of this point on the tnlandforms list and may fit the 'easternmost of five' description better; check before using the column as this tower's history. The record's 'GFC US 101' register appears in no source (tnlandforms gives gfc-101). The NHLR and FFLOS Georgia lists do not include this tower. Two readable pages failed: the waynesboroga.com history page timed out and the Georgia historic newspaper 1940 page did not render, so the local newspaper archive is not checked. Status, access and staffing are unknown. The story is below the 120-word target because nothing else was found.
